Subject: Cohort credits transfer and invoicing question

Hi Naomi,

Quick question from our finance team — we ran a pilot with a small group of portfolio companies in Luma Labs' spring cohort. We were issued a block of promotional credits tied to the accelerator account, but two of the startups didn't fully onboard and have leftover credits.

Is there a supported way to transfer unused cohort credits from the Luma Labs master account to other portfolio company accounts (or issue them as separate promo codes)? The main concerns are:
- Legal/billing: would this require an invoice adjustment or credit memo on Redwood's side?
- Expiration/audit trail: we need a clear record per company for our audit and tax people.
- Rate limits/quotas: if credits are moved, does it change cap/usage behavior per sub-account?

I've attached a short spreadsheet showing the leftover amounts per company (Luma_Cohort_credits.xlsx).

Appreciate any guidance or a recommended process — if there's a policy doc we can share with our finance team that'd be ideal.

Thanks,

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet, that helps. Short answer: we can support a couple of approaches, but each has different operational and accounting implications. High-level options: 

1) Credit pooling + allocation (preferred for cohorts): we leave the credits on the Luma master account and create internal allocations to portfolio sub-accounts in our billing system. That preserves one promo grant for audit purposes and gives each company separate usage records. It requires a short manual step on our side but no invoice reversal.

2) Issue separate promo codes to individual companies: we can generate one-time promo codes for the exact leftover amounts. That gives each startup direct ownership of the credit balance but will create multiple promo grants in our system (still auditable).

3) Credit memo / invoice adjustment: if Luma wants the credit removed from the master invoice and re-billed (or refunded) to redistribute, we can create credit memos but that is heavier — extra finance approvals and may delay availability.

Before we proceed I'd like a quick clarifying question: are the leftover credits meant to stay under Luma's corporate umbrella (so Luma retains control) or should they be fully assigned to each portfolio company's billing profile? If it's the latter, option (2) is cleaner for the startups.

I'll loop in Aditya from Sales to confirm how promo issuance impacts our quota and any discounting rules — Monica and I can then follow up with a brief process doc and a one-page policy draft for your finance team.

Naomi Feldman

Looping in from the pricing side — good context everyone. A few operational notes and constraints we've seen: 

- Promo issuance vs allocation: issuing promo codes (option 2) is faster (we can spin codes immediately) but creates discrete promo grants which show up on partner reporting. Pooling (option 1) is slightly more operational work for us (we maintain the master grant and attach internal allocations), but it keeps the legal grant singular which some partners prefer.
- Expiration: all promotional grants default to a 12-month expiry unless otherwise specified at grant time. If Luma needs a different expiry, we can set that per grant but it requires a written request and legal sign-off for longer windows.
- Quotas/limits: moving credits does not technically change compute quotas; pricing applies at token usage. However, for sub-accounts we recommend setting soft spend alerts to avoid surprises.
- Finance: if you require an on-record transfer (credit memo), our finance team will need the original grant id, the target billing ids for each startup, and signatures on a transfer form. That route takes 5-10 business days.

Attached is a short draft policy we use internally for partner credit movements (credit-transfer-policy-draft.docx). Suggestion: unless Luma's auditors insist on a credit memo, go with option 1 (pool + allocation) for minimal friction.

If that works, Naomi/Monica — can you confirm the exact billing IDs for the two startups and whether Luma wants expiry modified? Emma — if you can confirm ownership preference, we'll prepare the allocations and a short confirmation PDF for your records.

Thanks,

Proposed approach (recommended):
- We will keep the existing promo grant on the Luma master account and create allocations to each portfolio company for the leftover amounts (option 1).
- Allocations will be recorded with a unique allocation id per startup and will appear as separate line-items in usage exports for audit purposes.
- Expiry: keep standard 12-month expiry unless Luma requests an alternate window in writing.

What we need from Luma to proceed:

2) Provide target billing IDs for the two startups: Beacon Labs (billing id) and EmberAI (billing id).
